Coverage guard: 2 gap(s); corrective re-draft...

- Uncovered claim 'The forecast missed materially during the quarter' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim states the forecast MISSED (actual came in below the forecast). AC2 uses target_pct=107, which asserts actual was 107% of forecast — i.e., the forecast was BEAT, the opposite direction. A criterion whose parameters contradict the claim's stated direction cannot prove the claim false when false; the miss is unverified. The existing forecast_vs_actual check can express this claim but the drafted parameters are wrong/contradictory. (consider check: forecast_vs_actual)

- Uncovered claim 'Deals subsequently slipped into the following quarter' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim asserts deals slipped (slippage increased) into the following quarter. AC5 uses min_increase_pp=12, which requires a 12pp increase — a magnitude not stated or supported by the story. A claim that deals slipped by any meaningful amount cannot be disproven by a criterion demanding a specific 12pp jump. The existing slippage_trend check can express this claim but the drafted parameter is an unsupported magnitude. (consider check: slippage_trend)
Drafted 6 criteria: AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6
Coverage guard: 3 note(s) - proceeding:

[note] Uncovered claim 'exposing a forecast intelligence issue rather than a pure pipeline generation problem' [QUALIFIER]: This is a comparative narrative conclusion attributing the miss to forecast intelligence rather than pipeline generation. AC6 (creation_volume_trend) measures pipeline creation volume, which relates to the pipeline-generation side, but the claim's substance is the relative attribution between two root causes — a diagnostic judgment that no single metric primitive can express. The uncovered element is the narrative qualifier, not a measurable metric.

[note] Uncovered claim 'The forecast missed materially during the quarter' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim states the forecast MISSED (actual fell below forecast). AC2 uses target_pct=106, which asserts actual came in 6% ABOVE forecast — this directly contradicts the claim's stated direction. The forecast_vs_actual check CAN express this claim, but the drafted parameters are inverted, so the criterion would not fail when the claim is false. A correct criterion would target a value below 100% (e.g. target_pct around 94-97) to verify the miss. (consider check: forecast_vs_actual)

[note] Uncovered claim 'Managers included earlier-stage opportunities to offset pipeline gaps' [PARAMETRIC]: The claim's substance is that commit pipeline increasingly contains opportunities lacking genuine engagement (earlier-stage deals pulled in to fill gaps). commit_no_engagement_share is the existing check designed to measure exactly this. AC4 uses stage_aging (stale-opportunity aging), which measures how long deals sit in stages, not whether commit is inflated with non-engaged earlier-stage opportunities — wrong entity and wrong metric. No criterion measures the commit composition substance. (consider check: commit_no_engagement_share)
